newsitem.title: LATVIA: SPECIAL PERMIT FOR VOUCHER TRADE SCRAPPED.
newsitem.headline: SPECIAL PERMIT FOR VOUCHER TRADE SCRAPPED.

text.p: The government has scrapped rules which say companies trading privatisation vouchers need special permits, Dienas Bizness newspaper said on Wednesday.
To trade vouchers, a licence costing 100 lats earlier had to be purchased and two certified experts were needed.

"Any individual will now be able to accumulate vouchers in an account ahead of the privatisation agency or a local council decision on voucher privatisation of a particular enterprise," Economy Minister Guntars Krasts was quoted as saying.
Cabinet rules now provide that a bank which has opened the account of a voucher seller guarantees the delivery to the buyer and payment to the seller.
The valuation procedure of mutual investment funds has also been changed by the cabinet, the newspaper added.
The funds will now be valued in accordance to the market price of vouchers compared to the current system of using their nominal value of 29 lats.
